open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity and read_spooled_file
open_points.text: M22 says "Substitution: equal facts are the same spooled file" after listing digest, size, media type and disclosure class among its facts, while State 5 says "A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey)" and read_spooled_file calls that position tuple "its identity".
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile's identity the producing-position tuple alone, or all M22 meaning facts including content and class?
options: Use only (run_id, producer_node_id, map_index, attempt_number, producer_port, list_index) as identity and treat the other facts as attributes.
Use every M22 fact as the identity and require callers to provide digest, size, media type and class.
Define a positional lookup key distinct from the value identity and state which one records use.
open_points.default_guess: Use the producing-position tuple as the identity because State 5 lookup and replacement rules depend on it.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes and surface JSON parsing
open_points.text: The operation takes "One JSON value" but must refuse "a duplicate key"; separately, surface "turns every JSON text a request carries ... into its canonical form" before another module sees it.
open_points.question: What representation reaches canonical_bytes so it can detect duplicate object member names before ordinary JSON decoding discards them?
options: Pass raw JSON text or tokens to canonical_bytes.
Pass a duplicate-preserving parsed representation.
Require surface's parser to reject duplicates before calling canonical_bytes, leaving canonical_bytes unable to report that condition itself.
open_points.default_guess: Use a duplicate-preserving parse and reject duplicate names during canonicalization.

open_points.subject: installation.load_installation JSON object
open_points.text: The configuration must be "one JSON object with exactly the installation's fields", but the text does not say how duplicate member names in that object are handled.
open_points.question: Is a configuration containing the same JSON member name more than once invalid, and at which listed start check is it refused?
options: Reject every duplicate member name as invalid JSON/configuration shape.
Use the parser's selected value and continue validation.
Reject duplicates only for explicitly unique collections such as services and agent names.
open_points.default_guess: Reject every duplicate member name during the JSON-object check.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances
open_points.text: It refuses when a manifest record "fails a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5)", but A08 rule 5 mixes service-record checks, a named operation's checks, proposal-port checks and instance checks; check_installed_instances receives no operation or proposal ports.
open_points.question: Exactly which A08 rule 5 checks are performed on a service manifest during startup, and whether malformed unused capabilities stop startup?
options: Check only the service-level envelope and duplicate capability names, then the selected instance headers needed for the credential collision check.
Validate every capability's operation-level record facts and stop for any malformed capability.
Validate only the selected instance and required headers, ignoring capability records at startup.
open_points.default_guess: Check the service-level envelope and duplicate capability names, plus only the selected instance facts needed for header collision.

open_points.subject: trial execution output size
open_points.text: sandbox.execute_function applies the contract's output_bytes bound, while record_trial_execution writes StoredValues for value outputs; stored_value_bytes_max is smaller and M07 names detail_code value_too_large, but try_implementation and submit_implementation do not say when or how an otherwise successful trial output over stored_value_bytes_max is classified.
open_points.question: What outcome and detail does a trial receive when a valid function value output fits output_bytes but exceeds stored_value_bytes_max, and does that check precede expected-output comparison?
options: Record contract_violation with value_too_large before expected-output comparison and store no output value.
Record output_mismatch when expected output differs, otherwise contract_violation with value_too_large.
Allow the oversized StoredValue because output_bytes was satisfied.
open_points.default_guess: Record contract_violation with value_too_large before expected-output comparison and do not store the oversized value.

open_points.subject: service response diagnostic versus detail code
open_points.text: A09 says an unused response body is kept, bounded, as failure_detail; State 5 also requires closed details such as redirect_not_followed and value_too_large, while NodeExecution M23 has only failure_detail and no separate detail-code field.
open_points.question: For outcomes such as a read 3xx or an oversized 2xx output, does the NodeExecution store the closed detail code, the response-body diagnostic, both in separate fields, or a specified combination?
options: Store the closed detail code as failure_detail and discard the body diagnostic for these outcomes.
Add separate detail_code and failure_detail outputs, with the code fixed and the body diagnostic optional.
Store the bounded body in failure_detail and expose the closed code only as a derived result.
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate closed detail_code and optional bounded failure_detail so callers can act on the code without losing diagnostics.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.send_prepared_request for bindings without outputs
open_points.text: The operation says a binding without output ports has "none ... whose body is ignored", while A09 requires such a body to be read up to service_response_bytes_max and requires every body to be searched for a verbatim credential echo; an oversized or credential-echoing 2xx body is contract_violation.
open_points.question: For a binding without output ports, which body processing still occurs before the body is otherwise ignored?
options: Always enforce the response ceiling and credential-echo scan, but skip JSON parsing and output extraction.
Ignore the body completely, including its size and credential contents.
Enforce the size ceiling but do not scan for a credential echo.
open_points.default_guess: Enforce the size ceiling and credential-echo scan, then skip parsing and output extraction.

open_points.subject: inter-module refusal propagation
open_points.text: The convention says "Between modules, a refusal is the same pair (code, reason)" and surface returns it unchanged except internal_error and stop_required, but effects.reach_operation_element says "any refusal or error of a module it calls that is not one of those is internal_error"; operation_element_conclusion similarly says a failed read is internal_error despite the global rule that a missing record is unknown_reference "whatever operation looked it up".
open_points.question: When an internally called operation returns an unexpected refusal such as unknown_reference or an attempt-ordinal refusal, must the caller propagate it unchanged or translate it to internal_error?
options: Translate failures of internally derived references and invariants to internal_error; preserve refusals only for caller-supplied references and declared domain checks.
Propagate every refusal pair unchanged between modules as the convention states.
Specify the translation separately for each callee and failure code.
open_points.default_guess: Translate failures involving trusted internal facts to internal_error and preserve refusals arising from caller-supplied references.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file refusal effects
open_points.text: The general convention says "A refusal is decided before the operation's first store change, so it writes nothing", but spool_file says a ceiling refusal keeps nothing "of any file that attempt spooled before", deleting files published by earlier spool_file calls.
open_points.question: Is cleanup of previously published provisional files an allowed state effect of a refused spool_file call, or must the caller perform cleanup after receiving a side-effect-free refusal?
options: Make spool_file's ceiling refusal an explicit exception that atomically removes all provisional files of that attempt.
Have spool_file refuse without deleting earlier files and expose a separate cleanup operation.
Buffer all files for an attempt and publish them together so the refusal occurs before any publication.
open_points.default_guess: Declare spool_file an explicit exception that removes all provisional files of the same attempt on a ceiling refusal.

open_points.subject: store.open_store symbolic-link boundary
open_points.text: open_store enforces "no symbolic link anywhere", while A18 speaks of links in the data directory and files opened within it, without stating whether symbolic links in ancestor components of the configured data-directory path are included.
open_points.question: Which symbolic links make open_store refuse: the data-directory entry itself, every component leading to it, entries beneath it, or some combination?
options: Reject symbolic links in every path component leading to the data directory and anywhere beneath it.
Reject the data-directory entry and anything beneath it, but allow symbolic links in ancestor components.
Reject only entries found beneath an already opened data directory.
open_points.default_guess: Open component by component without following links and reject a link in any component or descendant.
